title: Nawab cured, celebrates the Khalsa, and summons Subeg Singh

blocks.text: This page closes the Kashmir precedent by recalling that even a ruler who had despised Hindus was told to submit to the symbolic touch of a Hindu’s shoe strapped on to the Nawab’s head. The old story mirrors Lahore closely and prepares the reader to see the Nawab’s relief as proof that the Khalsa Panth had cured him through a power the state could not command.

Back in Lahore, the restored Nawab began speaking openly of Sikh truth and of Guru Nanak's Karah Parshad, acknowledging that the Panth had answered him where his own camp had failed. The city illuminated at night in celebration, and the mood in court shifted from mockery to astonishment.

With that public change of heart, Subeg Singh summoned to the royal court became the key intermediary between the Nawab and the Sikhs. The page serves as a hinge between miraculous relief and the administrative concessions that soon follow.
